statements.t: “Based on data generated to date, we continue to believe PMN310 offers a differentiated approach by selectively targeting the most toxic and destructive form of amyloid-beta, the oligomers.

“With PRECISE-AD closing out its final stage of patient visits, we look forward to reporting topline data in the first quarter of 2027, which will include safety, biomarker and clinical efficacy measures.

PMN310’s Fast Track Designation allows for more frequent engagement with the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA), and we plan to request a meeting with the agency next year, after the full data set has been analyzed.

In parallel, we are advancing development of a subcutaneous formulation of PMN310 and preparing for a registrational study that, subject to FDA feedback, we anticipate initiating toward the end of 2027.”

The Company’s proprietary target discovery engine, EpiSelect™, has been shown to predict novel targets known as Disease Specific Epitopes (DSEs) on the molecular surface of misfolded proteins that cause neurodegenerative and other misfolded protein diseases, including Alzheimer’s disease (AD), amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), frontotemporal dementia (FTD), multiple system atrophy (MSA), and Parkinson’s…

PMN310, the Company’s lead product candidate for the treatment of AD, is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody designed to selectively target toxic misfolded oligomers while avoiding monomers, fibrils and plaque, potentially reducing or eliminating amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA) liability associated with plaque binding.

risks.t: the risk that early or interim results may not be indicative of final or topline results
